bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42508338 (espeak-ng): Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42508338
bug_description.normalized: The staged 405-byte ssml-fuzzer witness is passed to `espeak_Synth` in SSML mode. During SSML tag handling, `GetVoiceAttributes` derives a new voice identifier that resolves to a variant voice file under `espeak-ng-data/voices/!v/`, and `SpeakNextClause` later calls `LoadVoiceVariant` on that identifier. `LoadVoiceVariant` then invokes `LoadVoice(buf, 0)` on the `!v/*` file as if it were a normal base voice. Inside `LoadVoice`, stack buffer `phonemes_name[40]` is never initialized for this path: variant voice files contain `language variant`, so `V_LANGUAGE` hits the `strcmp(language_name, "variant") == 0` early break before the usual `strcpy(phonemes_name, language_type)` assignment, and those files also have no `phonemes` directive. At end of parsing, the code still executes `SelectPhonemeTableName(phonemes_name)` and, on failure, `fprintf(stderr, "Unknown phoneme table: '%s'\n", phonemes_name)`. Treating the uninitialized array as a C string makes `fprintf` read past the 40-byte stack object, and ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow read at `src/libespeak-ng/voices.c:917`.

source.code: attrcopy_utf8(ssml_sp->language, lang, sizeof(ssml_sp->language)); attrcopy_utf8(ssml_sp->voice_name, name, sizeof(ssml_sp->voice_name)); if ((value = attrnumber(variant, 1, 0)) > 0) value--; ssml_sp->voice_variant_number = value; ssml_sp->voice_age = attrnumber(age, 0, 0); ssml_sp->voice_gender = attrlookup(gender, mnem_gender);
source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled SSML tag state that drives the vulnerable path. `GetVoiceAttributes` copies the current tag's voice-selection attributes into the SSML stack frame that is later resolved into a concrete voice identifier.
source.value_from: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the exact staged 405-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42508338/poc` (sha256 `9a53d422c0f6e08e24579c787e98972b1e4c4d12b8453bf614db474606bf46c8`) to `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c`, which copies the bytes, appends one NUL byte, and calls `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML` at `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c:63-68`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The concrete vulnerability-relevant state is the newly selected voice identifier stored in `current_voice_id`. The later `LoadVoiceVariant` frame and the local voice-file inventory show that, for this witness, the identifier resolves to a bare `!v/<variant>` voice file that will be loaded as a normal voice.

sink.description: ASan sink. `fprintf` treats `phonemes_name` as a NUL-terminated C string after the post-parse phoneme-table lookup fails, so it reads past the 40-byte stack buffer until it encounters a zero byte.
sink.note: The saved ASan frame layout shows `phonemes_name` at `[368, 408)` in `LoadVoice` and reports the first invalid byte at offset `408` during this call, with `READ of size 42` in `fprintf`.

root_cause.description: The stack buffer `phonemes_name` is declared without initialization even though later logic may skip every assignment to it and still use it as a C string.
root_cause.note: On the vulnerable path, the selected `!v/*` file's `language variant` directive triggers the early break in `V_LANGUAGE`, so `strcpy(phonemes_name, language_type)` at line 634 never runs, and the variant-file corpus in this tree contains no `phonemes` directive to initialize the buffer later.

parser_admitted.condition: For the saved witness, SSML parsing reaches a voice-changing tag and sets `CLAUSE_TYPE_VOICE_CHANGE`, so `ReadClause` emits a concrete `voice_change` identifier that `SpeakNextClause` later loads.

fine_trace.code: attrcopy_utf8(ssml_sp->language, lang, sizeof(ssml_sp->language)); attrcopy_utf8(ssml_sp->voice_name, name, sizeof(ssml_sp->voice_name)); if ((value = attrnumber(variant, 1, 0)) > 0) value--; ssml_sp->voice_variant_number = value; ssml_sp->voice_age = attrnumber(age, 0, 0); ssml_sp->voice_gender = attrlookup(gender, mnem_gender);
fine_trace.note: The SSML parser copies the current tag's voice-selection attributes into the top SSML stack frame. The staged artifacts prove this tag later triggers a voice change, but because the witness is a binary fuzz testcase rather than a preserved text SSML document, the exact decisive field among `name`, `xml:lang`, `variant`, `age`, and `gender` is not recoverable from static evidence alone.

fine_trace.code: new_voice_id = VoiceFromStack(ssml_stack, n_ssml_stack, base_voice, base_voice_variant_name); if (strcmp(new_voice_id, current_voice_id) != 0) { strcpy(current_voice_id, new_voice_id); return CLAUSE_TYPE_VOICE_CHANGE; }
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled stack state from step 1 is resolved into a concrete voice identifier and stored in `current_voice_id`. Source inspection closes the later ambiguity: the crashing `LoadVoiceVariant` frame points to its first `LoadVoice(buf, 0)` call, and in this tree only `espeak-ng-data/voices/!v/*` files both parse as `language variant` and lack `phonemes`, so the selected identifier must be a bare `!v/<variant>` voice file. The saved artifacts do not reveal which exact variant name the binary witness selected.
When SSML processing ends the clause with a voice change, `ReadClause` copies the selected `current_voice_id` into the caller-provided `voice_change` buffer.
The completed clause returns the saved voice-change identifier to its caller, so `SpeakNextClause` receives a non-NULL `voice_change` pointer for the attacker-selected voice.
Clause-end voice-change handling loads the attacker-selected voice identifier once `voice_change` is non-NULL.

fine_trace.code: strncpy0(buf, vname, sizeof(buf)); variant_name = ExtractVoiceVariantName(buf, variant_num, 1); if ((v = LoadVoice(buf, 0)) == NULL) return NULL;
fine_trace.note: The selected identifier is copied into local `buf`, and `ExtractVoiceVariantName` strips only `+suffix` syntax. Because the selected identifier itself is already a `!v/<variant>` path, `buf` remains that variant-file name and the first `LoadVoice(buf, 0)` call opens the variant file as if it were a normal base voice. The saved ASan stack specifically reports `LoadVoiceVariant` at line 992, confirming the crash is on this first call rather than the later line-996 variant-only load.

The `LoadVoice` frame allocates `phonemes_name` on the stack without initializing it. `translator_name` and `new_dictionary` receive defaults later, but `phonemes_name` has no corresponding default assignment before the file parser starts.

When the selected `!v/*` file is parsed, its `language variant` directive makes `V_LANGUAGE` break out before the normal `strcpy(phonemes_name, language_type)` assignment at line 634. Local source inspection shows all 101 `espeak-ng-data/voices/!v/*` files in this tree have `language variant` and none has a `phonemes` directive, so this path leaves `phonemes_name` untouched for the rest of the load.

After file parsing finishes, the non-tone voice path still uses `phonemes_name` as a C string in `SelectPhonemeTableName` even though step 8 left it uninitialized. The lookup returns `< 0`, so execution takes the error-report branch immediately below instead of rejecting the missing initialization earlier.

ASan sink. `%s` makes `fprintf` continue reading `phonemes_name` until it finds a NUL byte, so the call runs off the end of the 40-byte stack object left uninitialized by steps 7 and 8. The saved report records `READ of size 42` here and pinpoints the first invalid byte immediately past `phonemes_name` at frame offset 408.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` only modify `CHANGELOG.md` language-list text and do not touch `src/libespeak-ng/voices.c`, `src/libespeak-ng/ssml.c`, `src/libespeak-ng/readclause.c`, or any other code on the saved ASan path. Stage 02 therefore has no staged patch-grounded remediation evidence for this crash.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the exact staged 405-byte input (sha256 `9a53d422c0f6e08e24579c787e98972b1e4c4d12b8453bf614db474606bf46c8`) to `/out/ssml-fuzzer`, which copies the bytes, appends one NUL byte, and calls `espeak_Synth` in UTF-8 SSML mode. That run reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 42` in `LoadVoice` while reporting `Unknown phoneme table` for the attacker-selected voice.

format.name: Exact staged ssml-fuzzer witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 405-byte fuzz testcase in `gt_results/arvo_42508338/poc` with sha256 `9a53d422c0f6e08e24579c787e98972b1e4c4d12b8453bf614db474606bf46c8`. The only verified trigger semantics are those proved by the saved run and source: `ssml-fuzzer` copies these raw bytes, appends one NUL byte, and submits them to `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`; during SSML tag handling, one parsed voice-selection state resolves to a bare `!v/<variant>` identifier; `SpeakNextClause(1)` then calls `LoadVoiceVariant` on that identifier; and the first `LoadVoice(buf, 0)` opens a `language variant` voice file with no `phonemes` directive, leaving `phonemes_name` uninitialized before the `%s` error report at `voices.c:917`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader class of SSML documents or identify which exact `!v/*` variant name inside the binary witness caused the selection.
